claim: fullWindowCount is only assigned inside the `if ts == ev.startTimestamp || selVS.Timestamp == nil` block, so for an @-anchored matrix selector under a non-step-invariant call (e.g. predict_linear(m[60s] @ 30, scalar(m))) IncrementSamplesAtStep adds 0 after step 0 instead of the retained window size; TotalSamplesPerStep goes from [5 5 5 5] to [5 1 1 1], breaking the existing totalQueryableSamples statistic and prometheus_engine_query_samples_total despite the stated invariant that they are unchanged.
raw: #1 🟠 High: `totalQueryableSamples` silently drops range-vector windows on `@`-modifier steps

claim: MergeSamplesReadFromSubquery in evalSubquery merges the child's SamplesRead into the parent, but the materialized subquery matrix is then counted again by the range-vector loop's IncrementSamplesReadAtStep at engine.go:2184, so samplesRead (and prometheus_engine_query_samples_read_total) is inflated ~2x for f_over_time(<subquery>) shapes; commenting out line 1874 turns SamplesRead 72 into 36 (= TotalSamples), the inflated values are baked into the new test expectations, and samplesRead > totalQueryableSamples contradicts docs/feature_flags.md:48.
raw: #2 🟠 High: subquery samples are counted twice in `samplesRead`

claim: Both new NewChildWithStepTracking call sites (engine.go:2396 and :1869) allocate two []int64 arrays sized by the subquery's step count for every subquery evaluation (~1.4 MB for foo[1d:1s]), uncharged against query.max-samples, and TotalSamplesPerStep is allocated even though the child's totals are discarded; previously stats.NewChild allocated nothing. Only under promql-per-step-stats with stats=all.
raw: #3 🟢 Low: per-step arrays now allocated for every subquery evaluation

claim: require.GreaterOrEqual(t, qs.Samples.SamplesRead, int64(0)) at api_test.go:983 (and :999) is tautological — SamplesRead is only ever incremented by non-negative counts, so the assertion passes even if the feature is wired to nothing; should assert a concrete expected value or at least require.Positive.
raw: #4 🟢 Low: new API assertions cannot fail

claim: IncrementSamplesReadAtStep adds to SamplesRead unconditionally but guards the per-step write with i < len(...), while sibling IncrementSamplesAtStep (:322-330) indexes unguarded — an out-of-range step would panic on the totals path but silently desynchronize SamplesRead from sum(SamplesReadPerStep) on the read path; also missing an i >= 0 check that IncrementSamplesReadAtTimestamp at :369 has.

claim: The subquery step-mapping loop divides by ev.samplesStats.Interval while offsetting by ev.startTimestamp (the evaluator's field); the two are equal today but mixing the stats object's copy of the layout with the evaluator's is fragile — ev.interval would be the consistent choice.
raw: Minor / Consistency: `promql/engine.go:2440` — the subquery step-mapping loop divides by `ev.samplesStats.Interval` while offsetting by `ev.startTimestamp`

claim: samplesRead does not dedupe under instant-vector lookback: evalSeries (engine.go:1773, :1796) increments read-count once per step, so a 10s-spaced series queried at 5s steps counts the same stored sample twice — inconsistent with the delta treatment of range-vector selectors, but documented as intended at docs/feature_flags.md:48, so treated as a design choice, not a defect.
raw: Considered But Not Flagged: `samplesRead` does not dedupe under instant-vector lookback.

claim: Subquery steps beyond the last outer step are clamped to numOuterSteps-1 (engine.go:2445-2447); the subquery evaluator produces points past the last outer window (e.g. t=220000 in the [60s:5s] test) which no outer step consumes, and they are attributed to the last step — deliberate and documented in the code comment; the wasted evaluation is pre-existing.
raw: Considered But Not Flagged: Subquery steps beyond the last outer step clamped to `numOuterSteps-1`
